title: The Lawyer Registry sets a high bar and is currently empty, which leaves the whole claim path without qualified counsel
content:
A.2.9.1.1.2.3.1 requires that "Lead Counsel, Lead Barristers, and Lead Trial Attorneys ... each have a minimum of ten (10) years of relevant legal experience," and A.2.9.1.1.2.3.2 adds that for litigious categories they "must have been Lead Counsel in at least 15 cases in the relevant area of law, type of process, and jurisdiction for which they are listed." General registry criteria add licensing, proven crypto or emerging-technology experience, absence of conflict, internal conflict-check processes, and a conflict-handling duty (A.2.9.1.1.2.2.1–.2.2.5).

The specificity is the binding constraint. Fifteen lead cases in the same area *and* process type *and* jurisdiction is a narrow intersection, and the covered areas (A.2.9.1.1.2.1) span securities enforcement, sanctions, IP trolling, employment, competition, data protection, and corporate tax across every jurisdiction where Sky is exposed.

The Active Data is unambiguous: "[t]here are no active legal counsels in the Lawyer Registry" (A.2.9.1.1.2.6.0.6.1). Since A.2.9.1.1.1.4.2.1.2 rejects a claim whose counsel fails registry criteria and A.2.9.1.1.2.3 requires RF-funded counsel to be listed as RF-qualified, no claim can currently reach approval with pre-vetted counsel — every claim must route through ad hoc vetting by a Committee that itself lacks quorum.

The conflict-handling rule compounds it: a conflicted firm must "transfer the matter to another LR registered Lawyer" (A.2.9.1.1.2.2.5), and with an empty registry there is no one to transfer to.
description: Lead counsel must have 10+ years and 15 lead cases in the exact area, process and jurisdiction; the Active Data records no active legal counsels, yet RF coverage requires registry-qualified counsel.
